subject.title: [Bug]: codex harness mirrored-session-history read fails for ephemeral sessions and on failover; one-shot cleanup retires shared app-server client while turns are in flight

question: Should this issue stay as the canonical fix scope for Codex `session_meta` mirror handling plus Active Memory/failover continuity, or should the remaining work be split across narrower existing issues?
rationale: Current main partially fixes the missing-file and shared-client lease mechanics, but the remaining `session_meta` and cross-runtime failover behavior depends on transcript ownership and replay policy that automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Keep canonical and narrow next proof
options.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella, require live or integration proof for Active Memory plus fallback, and decide whether `session_meta` should parse or quietly skip.

options.title: Split by owner boundary
options.body: Move Active Memory timeout evidence to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/100167, cross-runtime continuity to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/79047, and app-server close recovery to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/95547 before closing this as superseded.

options.title: Limit to warning cleanup
options.body: Treat Codex rollout JSONL as unsupported mirror input, change only the warning/debug behavior, and leave failover continuity to the existing cross-runtime feature discussion.

recommendation.title: Keep canonical and narrow next proof
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella, require live or integration proof for Active Memory plus fallback, and decide whether `session_meta` should parse or quietly skip.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the most recent partial fix and have recent Codex app-server cleanup history on the affected files.
